pr_body:
This PR refactors how the unicast group works in terms of when it is created, when it can be modified and how it is deleted. In a nutshell, the unicast group will now have the same lifetime as the underlying CIG. This gives us the same advantages and disadvantages of the CIG, and more tightly couples the unicast group to the ISO layer. 

This required significant rewrite of some of the underlying structures as ISO channels need to be allocated once the bt_audio_streams were added to the group, instead of when the streams were configured. 

Fixes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/45374
Fixes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/45741

issue_context.title: LE Audio: Allow unique `bt_codec_qos` for each unicast stream
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
The spec does not mandate that all streams in a unicast group for a specific unicast server shall use the same `bt_codec_qos` settings. 

The current API only supports supplying a single `bt_codec_qos` in the QoS function:
```c
int bt_audio_stream_qos(struct bt_conn *conn,
			struct bt_audio_unicast_group *group,
			struct bt_codec_qos *qos);
```

This should be made into an array, or somehow otherwise be attached to the individual streams. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Allow for more than a single `bt_codec_qos` for streams in a unicast group on a single server, i.e. different QoS settings for outgoing and incoming streams. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
N/A

**Additional context**
N/A
comments: In order to support the audio configurations defined by table 4.1 in BAP, we may also want to add an additional parameter to the QoS that can determine whether or not the audio stream should get it's own CIS or if it can share a CIS.

review_comments: This is nice! so now either the developer can create unicast_group with predefined settings or can fetch the settings during configuration.
Here, there is a change from a sum of SRCs and SNKs to a 2D array of GROUPs times STREAMs.  How does this relate to the rest of the changes?

It changed from
```
isos[CONFIG_BT_MAX_CONN][CONFIG_BT_AUDIO_UNICAST_CLIENT_ASE_SNK_COUNT + CONFIG_BT_AUDIO_UNICAST_CLIENT_ASE_SRC_COUNT];
```
to 
```
audio_isos[CONFIG_BT_AUDIO_UNICAST_CLIENT_GROUP_COUNT][CONFIG_BT_AUDIO_UNICAST_CLIENT_GROUP_STREAM_COUNT];
```

It is still a 2D array (as it was before). The difference is that the number of ISO channels we can support does not directly correlate the number of audio streams (as 1 ISO channel be used for 2 streams).
Is it intentional to no longer start scanning again at disconnection?
Or will that be taken care of by the main loop?
That is being taken of in the main loop as `scan_and_connect` is put inside that loop
